caption_en:
Two signatures changed this chart more than any war. Watch 1979.

Military spending as % of GDP (SIPRI via the World Bank, 2025):
Egypt 0.6%
Turkey 1.9%
Iran 2.1%
UK 2.4%
Lebanon 2.5%
USA 3.1%
Jordan 4.6%
Saudi Arabia 6.5%
Israel 7.8%
Syria: no data after 2010

1970: Israel 23.4%, Jordan 18.5%, Egypt 16.0%. Peace with Egypt (1979) and Jordan (1994). Israel fell to 4.3% in 2022, then rose to 8.5% in 2024 in the war that began on 7 October 2023.
Growth also shrank these shares, not only peace: a bigger economy makes the same army a smaller share.

Source: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database via World Bank, World Development Indicators, MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS, 1970 to 2025. The animation interpolates between years.
Photos: Egypt Israel peace treaty signing, 1979 (Yaakov Saar, GPO, CC BY-SA 3.0), Hussein, Clinton and Rabin, 1994 (White House, public domain), Arrow 3 test (US Missile Defense Agency, public domain), Riyadh (B.alotaby, CC BY-SA 4.0).
Made with AI tools. AI voice (Noam's own cloned voice).
caption_he: ב 1970 ישראל הוציאה 23% מהתוצר על ביטחון. אחרי השלום עם מצרים (1979) וירדן (1994) זה ירד ל 4.3% ב 2022. המלחמה העלתה ל 8.5% ב 2024, ו 7.8% ב 2025. מצרים היום: 0.6%. מקור: SIPRI דרך הבנק העולמי.

lines.line: Twenty three percent of everything Israel produced went to defence. That was in 1970.
This is the defence bill as a share of the economy. Lowest first.
In 1970, Israel, Jordan and Egypt all spend more than fifteen percent.
Egypt's bill falls and falls. Today, under one percent.
Syria disappears from the data after 2010, in its civil war.
By 2022, Israel is down to four point three.
Then October seventh, and war. In 2024 it jumps to eight and a half.
Saudi Arabia, six and a half. America, three.
What would the next peace deal pay for? Tell me in the comments.
Seven point eight percent. Down from twenty three.
